title: Role Orientation and Benefits Orchestration Playbook
author: Sofia Alvarez
body:
Overview

This playbook describes a unified approach to role orientation, benefits activation, and internal tools provisioning for new hires and transitioning employees at Redwood Inference. It is intended for people-ops partners, hiring managers, onboarding leads, and hiring-stage engineers who run orientation cohorts. The goal is to reduce time-to-impact, remove friction in benefits enrollment, and guarantee role clarity across teams.

Goals

- Provide a single, repeatable checklist covering the first 90 days for all role tiers (IC1–IC5, M1–M3, L1–L3).
- Ensure benefits and payroll enrollment are completed within 7 calendar days of start for 95% of hires.
- Deliver consistent access to required internal tools by day 1 for 90% of hires; day 3 for remaining hires.
- Establish role clarity artifacts (RACI, goals queue, success metrics) by the end of week 2.

Scope

Applies to: full-time employees, contractors longer than 90 days, and internal role transitions that change function (e.g., IC -> manager). Excludes short-term contractors (<90 days) and external temporary vendors.

Owner and Roles

- People Ops (owner): process, benefits orchestration, compliance checks
- Hiring Manager: role-specific training plan, 30/60/90 goals, weekly check-ins
- Onboarding Buddy: day-to-day questions, systems walk-through, culture signals
- IT/Access Team: accounts/provisioning SLA and escalations
- Security & Compliance: final access attestations for restricted data sources

Playbook summary (high level)

1) Pre-start (3–10 days before start)
   - People Ops sends welcome packet with benefits links, hardware options, remote-office stipend form, and required forms (I-9/identity verification where applicable).
   - Hiring Manager publishes a 30/60/90 draft in the Team Readme and assigns the onboarding buddy.
   - IT creates a provisioning request in the access tracker with target completion date (start day).

2) Day 0–1 (start day and first 24 hours)
   - Orientation session (90 minutes): culture, product one-pager, high-level org map, security basics.
   - Accounts: email, Slack, Redwood Console staging access, SSO, and laptop provisioning status communicated.
   - Benefits: new hire completes primary enrollment flow; People Ops validates elections.

3) Week 1 (fundamentals)
   - Team-level onboarding: architecture overview, team rituals, codebase tour (for engineers), customer portfolios (for CS).
   - Role clarity meeting: hiring manager and new hire agree 30-day objectives and acceptance criteria.
   - Internal tools training: guided sessions for Console, Cost Explorer, GitHub, CI runner access, and service dev keys where applicable.

4) Weeks 2–4 (ramp and contributions)
   - Assign first scoped-ticket: small, end-to-end task with mentoring.
   - Bi-weekly check-ins: manager and onboarding buddy present progress and blockers.
   - Benefits audit: People Ops runs enrollment reconciliation and follows up on missing items.

5) 30/60/90 Reviews
   - 30-day: confirm access, initial contribution, and adjust goals.
   - 60-day: deeper ownership of subsystem or customer workflow.
   - 90-day: readiness conversation and formal acceptance of role expectations.

Role Clarity Framework

Each new or transitioning role must have the following artifacts produced within two weeks:

- Role Definition (one paragraph): scope, top three responsibilities, key stakeholders.
- Success Criteria (3): measurable outcomes and acceptance criteria for the first 90 days.
- Escalation Path (one-liner): whom to contact for urgent blockers.
- Training Matrix (list): required trainings, optional deep-dive topics.

Onboarding Checklist (First 90 days)

Use this checklist to track progress. The hiring manager and the new hire must co-sign at 30/60/90 gates.

- Pre-start: welcome email, benefits packet, hardware request submitted, buddy assigned
- Day 0: orientation attended, accounts validated, Slack join, HR intro call
- Day 1–7: team tour, role clarity meeting, first ticket assigned, basic training modules completed
- Week 2: tools access verified, internal comms channels joined, security training completed
- Week 3–4: first PR merged or first customer engagement completed, feedback session
- 30-day: formal check-in and goal update
- 60-day: independent ownership of a small component, peer feedback collected
- 90-day: role acceptance, performance calibration input submitted

Benefits Orchestration (detailed)

People Ops is responsible for the end-to-end benefits activation workflow. The orchestration includes automated reminders and escalation steps to the hiring manager and payroll when enrollments are incomplete.

Key SLAs
- Benefits enrollment completed: target = 7 calendar days (95% of hires)
- Hardware provisioned: target = 5 business days (standard) or expedited within 48 hours if flagged
- Access provisioning (standard role): target = day 1 for common tooling; day 3 for specialized systems

Escalation flow for missing benefits or access
1. People Ops identifies missing enrollment at day 3 and sends first reminder.
2. Hiring Manager notified at day 5 if still incomplete.
3. At day 7, payroll and People Ops create an urgent case; access may be limited until compliance forms are submitted.

Internal Tools Access Matrix (example)

| Role / Tool                | GitHub | Redwood Console (prod-read) | Redwood Console (dev) | Slack | SSO | Cost Explorer | CI Runner | Customer CRM |
|----------------------------|--------|-----------------------------|------------------------|-------|-----|----------------|-----------|--------------|
| IC (Engineer, IC1–IC3)     | R/W    | R                           | R/W                    | R/W   | Y   | R              | R/W       | -            |
| IC (Senior / IC4–IC5)      | R/W    | R/W                         | R/W                    | R/W   | Y   | R/W            | R/W       | -            |
| Manager (M1–M3)            | R      | R/W                         | R                      | R/W   | Y   | R/W            | -         | R/W          |
| Customer Success / Sales   | -      | R                           | -                      | R/W   | Y   | R              | -         | R/W          |

Legend: R = read, W = write, Y = SSO-enabled, - = not required by default.

Tooling Provisioning Templates

- Access ticket template (IT): title, new-hire name, start date, role archetype, required systems, justification, approvals (manager + People Ops).
- Hardware request: form ID, preferred device, remote-office stipend opt-in, delivery address, contact phone.

Manager checklist for transitioning internal hires

1. Confirm role definition and update the Competency Map in the shared team folder.
2. Schedule role-transition kickoff meeting with People Ops and Security to review access changes.
3. Prepare 30/60/90 goals with measurable acceptance criteria.
4. Reserve shadowing sessions for knowledge transfer.

Compliance and Security Notes

- Restricted data access must not be granted until the mandatory security training is completed and signed off by Security & Compliance.
- For private deployments or customer-sensitive roles, an additional onboarding attestation form is required and the Access Team will run a manual review.

Metrics and Continuous Improvement

People Ops will report the following KPIs monthly to the People Ops leadership and cross-functional partners:

- Time-to-first-PR (median days)
- Benefits enrollment completion rate (7 days)
- Day-1 tooling access success rate
- 90-day role acceptance rate

Feedback channels

- New hire survey at day 7 and day 90 (anonymous, stored in People Ops survey system).
- Manager retrospective at 90-day gate.
- Quarterly playbook review with hiring managers and engineering leads.

Appendix: Example 30/60/90 template (one paragraph each)

30-day: "Understand the codebase, make one small production-safe change, and outline three learning goals for the next 60 days."
60-day: "Own a subsystem or customer workflow end-to-end and demonstrate reliability under mentorship."
90-day: "Independently drive improvements aligned to team objectives and participate in performance calibration."
